body: Note that this category-based design paves the way to [adding shortcuts to access specific items quickly](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11173), e.g. pressing `3`, then `1`, then `1` again to select `Prism 1x1` in the example screenshots.

That's an excellent new feature that will really ease building indoors level! What worries me is how easy/difficult it will be to set up the categories of 50 elements and more, like here: The thing is that most of the time, the user should be using a naming convention when creating modular assets for a grid, see for instance slide 84 and 87 of [The Modular Level Design of Fallout 4](https://media.gdcvault.com/gdc2016/Presentations/Burgess_Joel_Modular%2520Level%2520Design.pdf). Hence, I'm wondering if it could be more practical to encourage a naming convention and use the name of the asset to create the category tree. This way the "categorisation" can be done while creating the asset in Blender or Geometry Node, or Houdini, at the naming stage. For instance, we would have names like: `Bld_WoodP_Sm_Hall_2Way_01` Which would be converted to a tree: `Bld/WoodP/Sm/Hall/2Way/01` We could even imagine that the user provides a mapping "short name" to "long name" and we could convert the above to: `Building Kit/Wood Panel Variant/Small/Hallway/2-Way/Variant-01` Also, looking at this example, I think that we should be able to filter on multiple levels. For instance, we should be able to filter on "Small" and "2-Way" as in: `*/*/Small/*/2-Way/*` This way I can see all assets that are 2-Way (corners), and small height, whether they are wood panels or concrete panels or jungle panels or else. Anyway, this PR is the start of something very exciting!! I will be testing it asap.

> I think that we should be able to filter on multiple levels.

That is a matter of adding more different wildcard filter combos to the `searched_string` filtering.

It currently has just search basics matching for contains. Someone could extend that later, e.g. copying from how the editor Node search and create stuff does it with scoring and keyword matching.

> I'm wondering if it could be more practical to encourage a naming convention and use the name of the asset to create the category tree.

No we are not doing that. You do not want to have your internal category id be forced the same as your asset display name. It is one of those things that the CreationEngine did in the worst possible way, we are not copying that.

> No we are not doing that. You do not want to have your internal category id be forced the same as your asset display name. It is one of those things that the CreationEngine did in the worst possible way, we are not copying that.

Interestingly, the slides I referred to are from Bethesda and they are the makers of the CreationEngine 😄 
This being said, they released world-class RPG games (e.g. Fallout, Morrowind, Skyrim) that use extensively grid-based modular assets, so we might want to learn 1 thing or 2 from their tool when designing the Gridmap! (even if what we learn is what not to do).

If I understand, in your experience, the way that CreationEngine is automatising/helping the creation of categories is not ideal. Can you give us a summary of their method and the main advantages and main disavantages of their method? From there, we might be able to come up with a better method?
